speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs (a) in 2021, what has been the average frequency of the different rehabilitation programme interventions provided in (i) prisons (ii) drug rehabilitation centres and (iii) halfway houses; (b) what are the minimum qualifications and training which prison counsellors must have; and (c) what criteria are used to assess the effectiveness of these programmes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: In prison and drug rehabilitation centres, inmates undergo psychology-based correctional programmes to change their negative thinking and behaviours and improve their pro-social skills to minimise their risk of re-offending.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Inmates may also undergo other types of programmes, such as family programmes, to help them build stronger bonds, employability and skills training, work programmes, education, release preparation and religious programmes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: For example, the psychology-based correctional programmes consist of individual and group-based sessions and take place one to three times a week, with varying intensity from a few weeks to a few months, depending on the inmates’ needs and risks.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Religious programmes happen on a weekly basis, while pre-release programmes take place towards the tail-end of an inmate’s sentence.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: SPS also partners halfway houses to provide community-based programmes to inmates.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Depending on the programmes that they conduct, SPS staff and partners have a wide range of qualifications.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: They are selected and recruited on the basis that they have the relevant competency and skillsets to deliver the programmes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: SPS evaluates the effectiveness of its rehabilitation programmes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: For example, SPS had conducted an evaluation of its high-intensity psychology-based correctional programmes, which included taking pre- and post-programme measures.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The findings showed that inmates who had completed the programmes showed reduced negative thinking patterns and were more confident to stay away from drugs and crime.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Inmate feedback on the usefulness of the programmes is also collected.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: SPS provides different programmes in prison to help inmates in their rehabilitation and prepare them for reintegration into the society.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Ultimately, there are other factors, such as having stable employment and positive pro-social networks, that will help in the successful reintegration of ex-offenders in the longer term.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: It would also depend very much on the individual’s personal motivation and desire to change.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Just a full disclosure, I am on the Board of Yellow Ribbon Singapore.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: In September last year, I asked a Parliamentary Question (PQ) on the rehabilitation challenges faced by elderly inmates and also, in the recent cuts in the Committee of Supply, I have asked on rehabilitation efforts.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The Minister of State mentioned about the various rehabilitation programmes, such as the release preparation, religious, work and family programmes.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I was just wondering, how many, in terms of percentage, of inmates actually attended those programmes in the last year, in 2021.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: For those who did not attend, what are the reasons for them not attending?

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: If so, what are the steps that SPS and the Ministry would be taking to enhance attendance in such programmes?

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: However, about 5% may, eventually, not attend the programmes due to motivation or mental health issues.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: About 30% of the inmate population as at end-2021 attended work programmes.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: For other programmes, such as educational, religious programmes, the participation ranges from about 5% to 60%, as it depends on the inmates' own needs and preferences.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: All inmates, even those who decide not to attend the programmes, can access – using tablet computers – rehabilitation materials like e-versions of psychology-based correctional programmes, motivational talks and various guides on regulating emotions and communication skills.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: At the halfway houses, all supervisees would have to go through a programme to reinforce the skills and concepts learned in prison, like what I shared in my answer earlier.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, as I also said earlier, while SPS provides various programmes to help inmates, there are also other factors that will help in the successful rehabilitation and reintegration of ex-offenders, such as having stable employment and positive pro-social networks.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: It would also depend a great deal on the individual's personal motivation and desire to change.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: In fact, that is always the message whenever I visit the prisons to meet the inmates.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: I will always remind them "while we will do our best to help you to rehabilitate as part of your rehabilitation and reintegration journey, at the end of the day, a large part of it depends on you".

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We will continue to support them, so that they are able to reintegrate into the society in a better and stronger way.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: One is that, if an inmate, for whatever reason – be it lack of capacity or any other reason – would like to attend educational, rehabilitative or religious programmes, but they find that they do not have access to those programmes, can they make a request to attend such programmes and will that be taken into consideration in giving them access to such programmes, if for any reason they do not have that?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Second supplementary question: it is my understanding, based on published, publicly available information, that SPS adopts a classification system for inmates based on what is seen as their propensity to be rehabilitated.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Rehabilitation is not only about giving them programmes.
